title: Five molecular steps to a potent BCL-xL inhibitor
subtitle: Compound 4 → 6 → 7 → 16 → 21, anchored to 3SPF and explicitly reconstructed where no deposited pose exists

sources.label: Design of Bcl-2 and Bcl-xL inhibitors with subnanomolar binding affinities

cues.title: 4 · a weak but useful crystal lead
cues.body: Compound 4 binds BCL-xL at 138 µM. Its tractable scaffold and exact 3SPF pose make it a structural starting point.

cues.title: First, find the exit vector
cues.body: The camera moves once, without orbiting, to the scaffold atom used to reach the complementary recognition element.
cues.detail: One restrained move · then hold on the chemistry

cues.title: Before · the Site 1 scaffold ends here
cues.body: Hold this atom in the center of the frame. The next state grows from this exact exit vector.

cues.title: After · 6 links two weak recognition elements
cues.body: A 10.6 Å linker joins the Site 1 scaffold to a complementary Site 2 fragment, producing a greater than 10,000-fold affinity gain.
cues.detail: BCL-xL Ki <1 nM · cellular IC50 still >10 µM

cues.title: Reveal the full linked molecule
cues.body: Only after the new connection is clear does the camera pull back to show the full two-site span.

cues.title: Next, isolate the linker carbonyl
cues.body: The rest of the molecule is context. The edit is the single carbonyl at the junction to the distal recognition element.
cues.detail: Pan to one local chemical decision

cues.title: Before · compound 6 contains this carbonyl
cues.body: Hold the carbonyl at screen center before changing the graph.

cues.title: After · 7 removes the linker carbonyl
cues.body: Removing the linker carbonyl shortens the connection to 9.9 Å while retaining subnanomolar binding and producing measurable cellular activity.
cues.detail: BCL-xL Ki <1 nM · cellular IC50 1.8–2.0 µM

cues.title: Now follow the non-interacting side chain
cues.body: A slow pan moves to the solvent-facing dihydroxybutyl substituent; the viewing direction stays fixed.

cues.title: Before · this side chain adds burden, not binding
cues.body: Hold on the attachment point and the group selected for truncation.

cues.title: After · 16 removes the non-interacting side chain
cues.body: The dihydroxybutyl group is truncated to methyl, reducing molecular burden while improving cellular potency.
cues.detail: BCL-xL Ki <1 nM · cellular IC50 0.43–0.65 µM

cues.title: Finally, move to the open hydrophobic pocket
cues.body: The camera tracks to the pyrrole position beside the remaining pocket volume.
cues.detail: Pan to the final local design hypothesis

cues.title: Before · the pocket beside compound 16 is unfilled
cues.body: Hold the attachment point at screen center before adding the ethyl group.

cues.title: After · 21 fills the remaining hydrophobic pocket
cues.body: An ethyl substituent fills a nearby hydrophobic pocket and the optimized inhibitor reaches 61–90 nM cellular activity.
cues.detail: BCL-2 and BCL-xL Ki <1 nM · reconstructed coordinates are a visualization hypothesis

cues.title: Five states, four local design decisions
cues.body: Link, simplify, truncate, and fill: the camera returns to context only after each chemical change has been shown at its own site.
